create.title: Smooth balanced endpoint small-gcd quarter-packet reduction
create.statement_tex: For a uniformly smooth balanced symbol T_A(R,L)=sum_(h,k) chi_4(h) A(h/L,k/L)e(R sqrt(hk)), 1<=L<=R^(1/2), one has sum_m r_L(m)^2 << L^2 log(2L); exact squares and R^(-1)-near-squares contribute O_epsilon(L^(1+epsilon)) absolutely; and gcd(h,k)>=L^(1/2) contributes O(L^(3/2)) absolutely. With a fixed smooth dyadic partition g=gcd(h,k) asymp G<L^(1/2), h=gu, k=gv, gcd(u,v)=1, Poisson in g gives T_G=G P_G/(2i), where P_G retains chi_4(u) and the signed difference of the 3/4 and 1/4 resonance packets. Therefore the weakest remaining small-gcd target is |sum_G G P_G| <<_epsilon L^(3/2)X^epsilon. The shellwise sum_G G|P_G| version is stronger. Sharp gcd cutoffs and the hard top denominator endpoint are excluded unless their boundary terms are controlled separately.
create.next_action: Prove the outside-absolute signed aggregate |sum_G G P_G| at the L^(3/2) scale for the actual smooth interior symbol. Retain chi_4(u) and the 3/4-minus-1/4 packet difference. Treat the hard top denominator block separately.

create.title: Localized fixed-profile first-annulus capacity
create.statement_tex: Let a prescribed real smooth denominator profile have a fixed one-sign spatial slice J bounded away from the moving hard endpoint, and let the odd frequency block be nonterminal with L<=H/4 and a fixed positive interior. For either residue class modulo 4 and either side of the first nearest-odd product annulus, the additionally localized subtotal P_(c,J) has Y-average absolute size >> D/L and hence has size >>D/L for some real X asymp Y. This obstructs taking absolute values or estimating such localized pieces separately. It is not a statement about the whole class subtotal, the moving hard endpoint block, a common X for both classes, or the full signed block.
create.next_action: Seek cancellation before separating residue classes, sides, annuli, or spatial slices. Do not turn a localized subtotal into a lower bound for the full signed block.

create.title: One-sided transform for the hard top denominator block
create.statement_tex: For the explicit top block w_end(d)=W(d/y) 1_(d<=y), y=floor(sqrt X), derive a one-sided Poisson or stationary-phase formula with its boundary term, or prove the required pointwise M2 bound directly, uniformly for 1<L<X^(1/4). Discrete BV alone does not justify the accepted smooth transform because W(1)=1 and the continuum profile jumps at t=1.
create.next_action: Derive the exact Euler/Poisson endpoint contribution for the real top profile and decide whether it is target-sized, cancels with the dual bulk, or requires a direct sine-kernel estimate.

update.statement_tex: Let y=floor(sqrt X). There is an explicit fixed nonnegative telescoping dyadic partition of 1<=d<=y into active bands w_D plus a bottom remainder such that every active D>=X^(1/4) has fixed-shell support, ||w_D||_infinity+sum_d|w_D(d+1)-w_D(d)|<=4, sum_d|w_D(d)|>=D/8 for sufficiently large X, and H_D=floor(DX^(-1/4)) satisfies (1/2)DX^(-1/4)<=H_D<=DX^(-1/4). The inactive remainder is supported on d<<X^(1/4) and costs O(X^(1/4)) before Fourier expansion. Every interior active band is a full fixed C_c^infinity rescaling; exactly one top band has a continuum endpoint jump at d=floor(sqrt X). Thus B1, W-1, TTY, and profile-side Fejer hypotheses are verified for every active block, while smooth Poisson applies only to the interior blocks.
update.next_action: Use the verified partition for B1, W-1, TTY, and Fejer profile inputs. Apply smooth Poisson only to interior bands; route the single hard top band through M9-M2-top-endpoint-transform.

reject.reason: The proof gives D/L only for a fixed one-sign endpoint-interior slice P_(c,J); sign-changing slices can cancel in the whole class subtotal.
The cell average requires a fixed active endpoint margin and does not control a profile slice concentrated at the moving cutoff d<=floor(sqrt X).
The sum_G G|P_G| estimate imposes cancellation separately in each gcd shell. Only the outside-absolute |sum_G G P_G| target is logically weaker than the character-erasing mean square.
The top continuum profile W(t)1_(t<=1) jumps at t=1, so the accepted smooth Poisson and packet identities do not apply without an endpoint term.
